Isn't this the bug we need to fix?

Since thresholdInterfaces is of type `std::array` and uses the `Severity` property value as its index, the D-Bus path is created twice during sensor initialization, as shown below:
```
"Thresholds": [
    {
        "Direction": "greater than",
        "Name": "upper critical",
        "Severity": 1,
        "Value": 14.364
    },
    {
        "Direction": "less than",
        "Name": "lower critical",
        "Severity": 1,
        "Value": 9.576
    }
],
"Type": "ADC"
```
This results in the following assignments:
```
thresholdInterfaces[1] = objectServer.add_interface(dbusPath, interface);
thresholdInterfaces[1] = objectServer.add_interface(dbusPath, interface);
```
In reality, the array only retains the last assignment, so during destruction only one interface is removed.
Therefore, this issue is not caused by the destructor but rather by the creation logic, where we need to validate whether an interface with the same Severity property has already been created.

SO the problem is ultimately that we don't have RAII on the interfaces, which is an understood problem.

We should be unregistering the threshold if it exists, not just aborting.

The stress test uses a simple script that repeatedly modifies threshold values in entity-manager, which causes dbus-sensors to repeatedly destroy and recreate threshold interfaces.

After many create/destroy iterations, VmRSS occasionally increases. This correlates with duplicate interface creation for the same severity, where only one instance is tracked and cleaned up.

The fix prevents duplicate add_interface() calls and avoids this repeated reconstruction issue.
Feels a bit messy, but that's also a product of the existing code.

@ed@tanous.net @vernon.mauery@gmail.com
Any comments on this one?

Is this an issue in practice?  I can't say I've ever seen this in an EM review, but sure.

The amount of duplication here is a little worrying. Should we abstract these operations to a common method?  I believe a lot of the thresholding things are already common.

During BMC stress testing, sensor thresholds are frequently modified.
Each modification causes dbus-sensors to reload the sensor and create a new D-Bus path.
This issue leads to a memory leak after repeated operations.
To avoid breaking the existing logic, we should first check whether the object already exists before calling the `add_interface` method on D-Bus.

Duplication doesn't exist as when the array element is assigned again, earlier object at that index will get destroyed. But, if earlier it was creating a new interface at same object path why it was not throwing an exception for duplication of dbus interface at the same object path.

In the current code path, when multiple thresholds with the same Severity are processed, add_interface() may be called multiple times for the same object path and interface name. sdbusplus does not always throw an exception on duplicate interface creation, so this can silently succeed.

However, only the last created interface is tracked and explicitly removed during destruction. Earlier interfaces are never removed, which can lead to inconsistent object server state and undefined behavior.

Since severity maps 1:1 to a D-Bus threshold interface, it is correct to ensure that the interface is only created once per severity level. The added check prevents duplicate registrations and avoids relying on implicit or undefined cleanup behavior.

`thresholdInterfaces` is a fixed-size container(array), not a map.
operator[] does not create new entries and simply returns the existing element, which is default-initialized to nullptr.
Therefore the current check is safe and has no side effects.

Won't this just result in the new config not being applied?

I'm really not clear on how this can happen given that this is the TachSensor constructor, thresholdInterfaces hasn't been touched at this point.  Wheren you tested this were, you able to see this log?
